newsitem.title: USA: Fed should have one mandate, be accountable - Melzer.
newsitem.headline: Fed should have one mandate, be accountable - Melzer.

text.p: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis President Thomas Melzer said on Wednesday the U.S. central bank should have one clear mandate -- achieve price stability -- and be accountable for policy results.
"Currently, the Fed does not have a clear, achievable policy mandate," Melzer told the National Bank of Commerce of Mississippi at a meeting in Starkville, Miss.

"We could eliminate a lot of this uncertainty (in financial markets) if the Fed were given a mandate that recognized what monetary policy can do, and what it cannot do," Melzer said. "In my view, monetary policy can reliably affect only the price level, so I favor a mandate that requires the Fed to pursue price stability."
The St. Louis Fed president noted one drawback of unclear policy goals is increased volatility in financial markets.
"I am convinced that uncertainty about the Fed's monetary policy goals and methods produces greater volatility in markets than would otherwise occur," Melzer said.

"A clear mandate to the Fed to preserve the purchasing power of the dollar would eliminate much of the current uncertainty about policy and provide a stable price backdrop for the efficient operation of our economic market," he added.

The Fed currently operates under a dual full-employment, anti-inflation mandate. A bill is pending in Congress to give the Fed the sole mission of achieving long-term price stability by targeting consumer inflation.
"Another source of uncertainty about the course of monetary policy stems from the Fed's fragile political independence," Melzer further noted.
The St. Louis Fed president also tied suggestions to reduce the Fed's independence to "the apparent lack of focus of monetary policy" rather than concern about Fed policy.
By law, the Fed chairman must testify before Congress twice a year about the economy and monetary policy. However, the Fed is not accountable for the results of its policy.

"The Fed should be held accountable as an institution for what it can, and should, achieve -- namely average price stability over time. Make the Fed's mandate explicit and achievable and accountability will be clear."
Melzer also reiterated the view that an overly stimulative monetary policy can only fuel inflation.
"Inflation can certainly impede growth," Melzer stated.

"Because monetary policy has the potential to boost output in the short run, some may be tempted to push for faster and faster growth by stepping on the monetary accelerator," he said. "Output may, indeed, go up for a time but, eventually, inflation will be the only outcome of our experiment."
Melzer also stressed "the view that monetary policy could 'fine-tune' economic activity turned out to be a mirage" in the 1960s and 1970s.
